handoff.purpose: Run node ids, validate task schema, build disposable worktree, apply overlay/patch, and define frozen Selection.

symbols.name: run_node_ids
symbols.note: Dedupes node ids, refuses primary checkout, batches pytest, solo re-runs unattributed nodes.

symbols.name: TestRunner
symbols.note: Type alias for injectable test runner; product path is run_node_ids.

symbols.name: REQUIRED_FIELDS
symbols.note: Tuple of required task fields: id, repo, base_revision, fail_to_pass.

symbols.name: validate_task
symbols.note: Returns list of schema problems; never raises.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: Delegates to daedalus.eval.tasks.is_correctness_task.

symbols.name: disposable_worktree
symbols.note: Context manager creating a git worktree via GitWorktreeManager; cleans up unless keep.

symbols.name: apply_test_overlay
symbols.note: Writes test files from test_revision into worktree via git show.

symbols.name: reference_patch
symbols.note: Computes git diff base..reference, excluding overlay paths.

symbols.name: apply_patch
symbols.note: Applies patch via git apply; returns error string or None.

symbols.name: Selection
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass storing base_revision, node id lists, overlay, gate, timeout.

claims.text: Batch first (one interpreter start, ~2.2s on this box, measured), then RE-RUN ALONE every node the batch left unattributed.
claims.why: Code calls _spawn_pytest once with all nodes, then iterates unattributed and calls _spawn_pytest per node.

claims.text: That fallback is not belt-and-braces, it is required: measured on this box, a single node id pytest cannot collect aborts the WHOLE invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs -- even with --continue-on-collection-errors.
claims.why: The exit-4 claim concerns pytest behaviour outside this chunk; the code does not assert or branch on rc==4.

claims.text: Without the solo re-run, one bad node id would turn every other node in the batch into not_run and the task into could_not_run.
claims.why: This is a counterfactual about the absence of the solo re-run; not observable in this code.

claims.text: worktree is refused if it is the primary checkout or inside it.
claims.why: Line 561 calls _refuse_primary_checkout(worktree, repo_root, 'pytest working directory') before running.

claims.text: Every schema problem with task, or []. Never raises.
claims.why: All accesses use task.get; type checks guard non-dict input; no unguarded indexing.

claims.text: An EMPTY fail_to_pass is an error, not an empty success: a task with no test that must go from red to green cannot fail, and a measurement that cannot fail is the exact defect harness._recall's vacuous 1.0 already demonstrated in this repo.
claims.why: REQUIRED_FIELDS includes 'fail_to_pass', and the loop appends 'missing or empty required field' when task.get('fail_to_pass') is falsy.

claims.text: A checkout of revision that is NOT the primary checkout.
claims.why: The context manager calls _refuse_primary_checkout(path, repo_root, 'disposable worktree') after creating the worktree.

claims.text: Delegates to daedalus.kairos.worktree.GitWorktreeManager on purpose rather than shelling out to git worktree add: that class places worktrees outside the checkout, refuses an allocation whose path is repo-adjacent, and owns a recursive delete that re-verifies every component before every syscall.
claims.why: The behaviour of GitWorktreeManager is in another module; this chunk only calls create_worktree, cleanup_worktree, reap_branches.

claims.text: Its cleanup is the ONLY delete this module performs; there is no shutil.rmtree here and there must never be one.
claims.why: This chunk contains no shutil.rmtree; only manager.cleanup_worktree and os.unlink in apply_patch.

claims.text: The branch ref that git worktree add -b writes into the shared .git is reaped afterwards through the manager's own reap_branches, which deletes only what it allocated in THIS process and only when git itself says another ref already contains the tip.
claims.why: reap_branches is in GitWorktreeManager; this chunk only calls it.

claims.text: Bytes are copied verbatim from git (git show <rev>:<path>), never decoded and re-encoded, so line endings and encoding are exactly what the commit holds.
claims.why: Code uses _git_read(..., 'show', f'{test_revision}:{rel}') and writes proc.stdout bytes directly.

claims.text: Raises FileNotFoundError if a path does not exist at that revision, and OverlayEscape if it would land outside the worktree.
claims.why: FileNotFoundError is raised on non-zero returncode; OverlayEscape would come from _safe_join, whose implementation is elsewhere.

claims.text: The task's own test files are EXCLUDED, because they are applied separately as the overlay -- if the reference patch carried them too, the 'after' run would be testing a tree the candidate path never produces, and the two arms would not be comparable.
claims.why: The args list appends f':(exclude){rel}' for each rel in exclude.

claims.text: A patch that does not apply is a could_not_run, never a not_fixed: 'the change was rejected by git' and 'the change did not fix the bug' are different facts about different things.
claims.why: The mapping from apply_patch's return value to could_not_run/not_fixed is in caller code elsewhere.

claims.text: Immutable (frozen dataclass, tuples not lists) and digested, so 'what was measured is what was declared' is checkable by a reader instead of being a claim in a docstring.
claims.why: Selection is @dataclass(frozen=True); fail_to_pass, pass_to_pass, test_overlay are tuple-typed; digest is referenced.

claims.text: digest covers all of it. Change any node id, the base, the overlay or the timeout and the digest changes, which is what lets correctness_gate refuse a task that was verified under one selection and presented under another.
claims.why: digest is not defined in this chunk; correctness_gate is elsewhere.

observations.what: run_node_ids checks len(unattributed) == len(nodes) == 1 and returns early, skipping the solo re-run for a single unattributed node.
observations.why: The docstring says the solo re-run is required, but the code explicitly bypasses it when the batch had exactly one node and it was unattributed.

observations.what: The containment update logic: containment = solo_containment if containment == 'none' else containment. If the batch containment was 'none' and a solo run reports a non-'none' containment, it adopts it; if batch containment was already non-'none', solo containment is ignored. This may mask a solo containment that differs from batch.
observations.why: The rule only replaces 'none'; it does not compare or merge other values.

observations.what: validate_task checks overlap of fail_to_pass and pass_to_pass, but the docstring says 'it cannot both fail and pass before the change' -- this check is about the same node id in both lists, which is a reasonable interpretation.
observations.why: The docstring's 'before the change' might also be read as a temporal claim; the code only checks set intersection.

observations.what: apply_test_overlay writes files with target.write_bytes(proc.stdout) but does not fsync; a crash could leave partial files.
observations.why: No fsync or atomic write is used, but this is a common pattern for ephemeral worktrees.

observations.what: apply_patch uses subprocess.run directly rather than the module's _spawn_pytest or a git wrapper; it does not use _git_read or _git_in_worktree, so it may not benefit from the same containment or validation.
observations.why: It shells out to git apply with cwd set to the refused worktree, but no containment or timeout beyond DEFAULT_GIT_TIMEOUT_S.

observations.what: reference_patch uses _git_read but does not verify the worktree is not the primary checkout; it only reads from repo_root.
observations.why: The docstring does not promise such a check, but other functions in this chunk do.

risks: run_node_ids | medium | Single unattributed node skips solo re-run, contradicting the docstring's requirement; could leave a node as not_run when a solo run might have succeeded. | Run a single-node batch with an unattributable node and see if the solo re-run is skipped.

run_node_ids | low | Containment update only adopts solo containment when batch was 'none', potentially ignoring a solo containment that differs. | Compare containment values from batch and solo runs with multiple unattributed nodes.
validate_task | low | Overlap check is set-based and does not consider ordering or duplicate entries within a list. | Feed a task with duplicate node ids in one list.
apply_test_overlay | low | No fsync on written files; crash could leave partial overlay. | Check whether GitWorktreeManager or later steps verify file integrity.
apply_patch | low | Uses subprocess.run directly without the module's containment wrapper; may lack the same safeguards. | Inspect _spawn_pytest for containment logic and compare to this call.
reference_patch | low | Does not refuse primary checkout; could read from the primary checkout if called that way. | Check callers to see if repo_root is always a non-primary path.
